title: Deforestation

source.name: Wikipedia — Deforestation
source.note: Đã rút gọn: chỉ giữ một số đoạn.

paras: Deforestation or forest clearance is the removal and destruction of a forest or stand of trees from land that is then converted to non-forest use. Deforestation can involve conversion of forest land to farms, ranches, or urban use. About 31% of Earth's land surface is covered by forests at present. This is one-third less than the forest cover before the expansion of agriculture, with half of that loss occurring in the last century. On average 2,400 trees are cut down each minute. Estimates vary widely as to the extent of deforestation in the tropics. In 2019, nearly a third of the overall tree cover loss, or 3.8 million hectares, occurred within humid tropical primary forests. These are areas of mature rainforest that are especially important for biodiversity and carbon storage.

By far, the direct cause of most deforestation is agriculture. In 2025 nearly 90% of global deforestation was caused by agriculture, with cropland expansion and pasture creation the primary drivers, this is up from more than 80% in 2012. Forests are being converted to plantations for coffee, palm oil, rubber and various other popular products. Livestock grazing also drives deforestation. Further drivers are the wood industry (logging), urbanization and mining. The effects of climate change are another cause via the increased risk of wildfires (see deforestation and climate change).

Deforestation results in habitat destruction which in turn leads to biodiversity loss. Deforestation also leads to extinction of animals and plants, changes to the local climate, and displacement of indigenous people who live in forests. Deforested regions often also suffer from other environmental problems such as desertification and soil erosion.

Another problem is that deforestation reduces the uptake of carbon dioxide (carbon sequestration) from the atmosphere. This reduces the potential of forests to assist with climate change mitigation. The role of forests in capturing and storing carbon and mitigating climate change is also important for the agricultural sector. The reason for this linkage is that the effects of climate change on agriculture pose new risks to global food systems.

Since 1990, it is estimated that some 420 million hectares of forest have been lost through conversion to other land uses, although the rate of deforestation has decreased over the past three decades. Between 2015 and 2020, the rate of deforestation was estimated at 10 million hectares per year, down from 16 million hectares per year in the 1990s. The area of primary forest worldwide has decreased by over 80 million hectares since 1990. More than 100 million hectares of forests are adversely affected by forest fires, pests, diseases, invasive species, drought and adverse weather events.

Deforestation and forest area net change are not the same: the latter is the sum of all forest losses (deforestation) and all forest gains (forest expansion) in a given period. Net change, therefore, can be positive or negative, depending on whether gains exceed losses, or vice versa.

questions.q: What does the first paragraph suggest about forest cover today compared with the past?
options: Forests cover slightly more land than before farming expanded
Forests now cover roughly a third less land than before farming expanded
Almost none of the loss of forest happened in the last hundred years
About 31 percent of all forest has disappeared in the last century
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: rừng hiện chiếm khoảng 31% đất liền, ít hơn một phần ba so với trước khi nông nghiệp mở rộng; một nửa mức mất này xảy ra trong thế kỷ qua.

questions.q: Why does the writer give special attention to rainforests in the humid tropics?
options: They lose trees faster than any other type of forest in the world
They are old rainforests vital for wildlife variety and carbon capture
They are the only forests that farming does not threaten at all
They supply most of the timber used around the world today
questions.explain: Đoạn 1: đây là rừng mưa trưởng thành, đặc biệt quan trọng với đa dạng sinh học và lưu trữ carbon.

questions.q: Which conclusion is supported by the second paragraph?
options: Mining has overtaken farming as the leading cause of forest clearance
Livestock grazing has very little effect on forests
Climate change is a more direct cause of deforestation than agriculture
Growing demand for goods such as coffee and palm oil can lead to forest loss
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: rừng bị chuyển thành đồn điền cà phê, dầu cọ, cao su…; nông nghiệp là nguyên nhân trực tiếp chính.

questions.q: How is deforestation connected with climate change, according to paragraph 4?
options: With fewer trees, less carbon dioxide is taken in from the air
Trees give off more oxygen when they are cut down
Young forests release more carbon than mature ones
Farmland absorbs more carbon dioxide than forest does
questions.explain: Đoạn 4: phá rừng làm giảm khả năng hấp thụ CO₂ của khí quyển.

questions.q: What trend do the figures in paragraph 5 reveal?
options: The rate of loss has risen steadily since 1990
Forest area is no longer shrinking anywhere in the world
Forest is still being lost, but more slowly than in earlier decades
Fires and pests are the only reasons that forest disappears
questions.explain: Đoạn 5: tốc độ mất rừng giảm từ 16 xuống 10 triệu ha/năm nhưng vẫn tiếp diễn.

questions.q: Why can the net change in forest area be positive even while deforestation continues?
options: New forest growth can exceed the area that is cleared
Deforestation is not counted in the calculation
Losses are measured only in tropical regions
Only plantation forests are included in the figure
questions.explain: Đoạn 6: net change = tổng mất rừng + tổng tăng rừng; dương nếu tăng nhiều hơn mất.

questions.q: The text suggests that agriculture causes more forest loss than all other causes put together.
questions.explain: Đoạn 2: nông nghiệp gây gần 90% nạn phá rừng toàn cầu → nhiều hơn tất cả nguyên nhân khác cộng lại.

questions.q: Most deforestation in tropical areas is carried out illegally.
questions.explain: Bài không nói về tính hợp pháp của việc phá rừng.

vocab.def: the removal of things from a place
the process of changing something into another use
vocab.ex: conversion of forest land to farms

vocab.def: the natural home of an animal or plant
the forcing of people to leave their home
the gradual wearing away of soil
the process by which land becomes desert

vocab.ex: depending on whether gains exceed losses

coll.ex: trees are cut down each minute

str.ex: By far, the direct cause of most deforestation is agriculture.
str.explain: By far nhấn mạnh mức độ vượt trội của một nguyên nhân.

str.ex: depending on whether gains exceed losses, or vice versa
str.explain: depending on whether A or B: kết quả phụ thuộc vào điều kiện.

str.ex: although the rate of deforestation has decreased
str.explain: although mở đầu mệnh đề nhượng bộ.

str.ex: down from 16 million hectares per year
str.explain: down from + số: cho biết mức trước đó cao hơn.
